article_title: vLLM 0.32.0 Drops Python 3.10, Stops Allowing Every CORS Origin by Default and Removes Cascade Attention

content_preview.title: vLLM 0.32.0 Drops Python 3.10, Stops Allowing Every CORS Origin by Default and Removes Cascade Attention
content_preview.summary: vLLM 0.32.0 requires Python 3.11 or later, restricts default CORS origins, removes cascade attention and fixes three security advisories, per its release notes.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The vLLM project published version 0.32.0 on October 18, according to the [vLLM v0.32.0 release notes](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/tag/v0.32.0). The notes describe the release as "814 commits from 363 contributors (121 new)". Its breaking-changes list includes dropped Python 3.10 support, CORS defaults that no longer allow every origin, and the removal of cascade attention. This briefing covers what operators of the inference engine need to check before upgrading, ...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured Briefing (640 words, range 300-800) with Overview, Breaking changes, Security fixes, New features and What We Don't Know. Operator-focused, appropriate technical depth, neutral tone, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read snapshots source-0.html.gz (v0.32.0 release) and source-1.html.gz (v0.31.0 release) from sources/2026-10/vllm-0320-.../ (status 200, suspicious_patterns null for both), then re-fetched the RAW release bodies live via the GitHub API (gh api repos/vllm-project/vllm/releases/tags/v0.32.0 and v0.31.0) and verified claim by claim. v0.32.0 (published_at 2026-10-18T06:50:48Z): quote '814 commits from 363 contributors (121 new)' verbatim; Python 3.10 dropped, 'the minimum is Python 3.11 (#60402)' verbatim, Build section 'Python 3.11-3.14 supported'; transformers>=5.16.1,<5.20.0 and tokenizers>=0.23.2 correct; CORS: 'Default CORS origins changed from `*` to none; set `--allowed-origins` for browser clients (#61009)', Security section confirms Python and Rust frontends; cascade attention removed, '--disable-cascade-attn still parses but only warns and will be removed in v0.33.0' (#61126) matches; torch.compile SP/AsyncTP passes and PassConfig.enable_sp/fuse_gemm_comms/sp_min_token_num match, model-level SP unaffected matches; max_tokens upper bound, Responses API renamed events, mamba_cache_mode=all removal, and the listed removed APIs all match. Security: GHSA-4hhp-h66f-j5j7 (static validation, VLLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_RENDER_TIMEOUT, user chat_template in chat_template_kwargs rejected), GHSA-q97c-p368-75c4 (tokenizer max_token_id off-by-one), GHSA-frvg-qw88-hww9 (VLLM_P2P_MAX_PEERS 128, HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_S 30, IDLE_TIMEOUT_S 300) match; the notes give no severity ratings or affected-version ranges and the article names no CVE, so the article's statement is true and it claims nothing more. 64-level JSON schema 400, raster-format image allowlist and signed shared-memory handles match. Features: /v1/systemone quote verbatim, hf tool/reasoning parser, NVFP4 KV on SM8x/SM12x, GLM-5.x FP8 KV on SM100, vllm download-kernels, vllm preload --preload-autotune, least-loaded API worker '43-85% more req/s on short requests (Qwen3-0.6B, 32 input / 1 output tokens) in the PR's benchmark' verbatim and properly attributed to the PR benchmark, EmbeddingGemma 2, MiniCPM-V 4.7, Nemotron 3.5 ASR, MRV2 default on ROCm all match. v0.31.0 (published_at 2026-10-05T06:44:55Z): '717 commits from 307 contributors (96 new)' verbatim and genuinely 0.31.0's; the comparison is not invented. Nothing attributed to 0.32.0 belongs to 0.31.0 (0.31.0 notes contain no Python 3.10, CORS default or cascade attention removal items). Dates October 18 and October 5 match. No individual PR/contributor credits are named in the article. Both body URLs are in article.sources (no orphans). Internal links /article/2026-10/02-vllm-030-... and /article/2026-10/06-vllm-031-... use the correct singular form, resolve to existing published articles, and are described accurately (0.30 and 0.31 releases covered earlier in October: Oct 2 and Oct 6).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, date, quote, flag name, env var and default checked against raw release bodies; no discrepancies, no fabricated specifics. Minor phrasing note: 'must set --allowed-origins' slightly strengthens the notes' 'set --allowed-origins for browser clients' but is substantively equivalent.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; benchmark figure explicitly attributed to the PR; What We Don't Know section is honest about single-source basis.
editor_notes.originality: New topic: first Herald coverage of vLLM 0.32.0. Prior vLLM 0.30 and 0.31 articles are distinct releases and are linked as context. No duplicate.
recommendations: Optionally name the PR numbers for the three breaking changes headlined in the title (#60402, #61009, #61126).
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced first-party release briefing; all checks pass and all claims verified against raw release bodies. Integrity checks passed (hash, signature, v3 fields). Featured candidacy: 1 - accurate release coverage with breaking changes and security defaults relevant to a defined audience of vLLM operators
